title: Summer upwelling, wind jet and cold filament off southern Vietnam
query: Using the supplied CMOMS daily temperature, velocity and chlorophyll for 2011-2020 and NOAA blended monthly winds for 2003-2020, test the following findings of Xie et al. (2003, Journal of Geophysical Research, doi:10.1029/2003JC001867) on summer upwelling off southern Vietnam: (1) the southwest monsoon forms a wind jet off the southern tip of Indochina, whose strong wind-stress curl drives coastal and open-ocean upwelling; (2) in July and August an anticyclonic eddy to the southeast carries the cold coastal water offshore as a cold filament; (3) the filament's centre lies north of the wind-speed maximum, so open-ocean upwelling helps cool the surface; (4) a tongue of high chlorophyll is collocated with the cold filament; (5) the filament interrupts summer warming, giving a semi-annual SST cycle, and interannual SST variance peaks over the climatological filament. Give a verdict for each finding (reproduced, partly reproduced, not reproduced, or not testable with the supplied data) with quantitative evidence, and explain differences from the paper, which used satellite data.
